raw_segments.text: The heir of every immediate vassal of the crown paid a certain duty, generally a year's
rent, upon receiving the investiture of the estate.
If the heir was a miner, the whole rents of the estate, during the continuance of the
minority, devolved to the superior without any other charge besides the maintenance of
the miner, and the payment of the widow's dower, when there happened to be a dowager
When the miner came to be of age, another tax, called relief, was still due to the
superior, which generally amounted likewise to a year's rent.
A long minority, which, in the present times, so frequently disburdens a great estate of
all its encumbrances, and restores the family to their ancient splendor, could in those
The waste, and not the disencumbrance of the estate, was the common effect of a long minority.
